entities.summary:
Alexander of Lincoln was a medieval English Bishop of Lincoln and a member of an important administrative and ecclesiastical family. Born into the influential family of the Earls of Lincoln, he was educated at Laon and served in his uncle's diocese as an archdeacon in the early 1120s. In 1123, he was appointed Bishop of Lincoln, a position he held until his death in 1148. As Bishop, Alexander played a significant role in the governance of Lincoln Cathedral and the surrounding diocese, implementing various reforms and initiatives to promote the growth of Christianity in the region. His legacy as a religious leader and administrator has endured, with many of his contributions to the cathedral's architecture and liturgy still evident today. The appointment of Alexander of Lincoln as Bishop of Lincoln marked a significant turning point in the history of the diocese, one that would have far-reaching consequences for the development of Christianity in England.

The appointment of Alexander of Lincoln as Bishop of Lincoln was a result of the efforts of his uncle, Roger of Salisbury, who had previously served as Chancellor of England under King Henry I. The appointment was also influenced by the growing power of the English monarchy, which had begun to assert its authority over the church in the years leading up to Alexander's appointment. As Bishop, Alexander worked closely with the king to promote the interests of the church and to further the goals of the English monarchy.
